newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-MONACO PUNISH HAMBURG WITH THREE SECOND HALF GOALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO PUNISH HAMBURG WITH THREE SECOND HALF GOALS.

text.p: Monaco woke up after the break to crush Hamburg of Germany 3-0 in the first leg of their UEFA Cup third round tie on Tuesday.
The game, on a cold, wet night in the principality, only really came to life in the 48th minute after Brazilian Sonny Anderson headed the ball home from a cross by young defender Lilian Martin.

Monaco, who had looked sluggish throughout a dull first half, then took control of the game and Hamburg goalkeeper Richard Golz was forced into making a good save three minutes later from a powerful Victor Ikpeba header.
The Nigerian striker, in brilliant form, eventually made it 2-0 with a close range effort after 70 minutes.
Monaco kept attacking and in the 76th minute their efforts paid dividends again when defender Patrick Blondeau added the third with a shot from inside the penalty area.
